items.rationale: Theft damage to the stolen bike is covered under 2.3.1(b) and 7.1.1(b). It falls in the mobility class, so the EUR 500 aggregate sub-limit (4.2.2) applies; total indemnifiable cost of about EUR 1,060 is scaled by roughly 0.47.
Covered theft damage under 7.1.7(b). Market price of about EUR 145 is scaled rateably under the EUR 500 sub-limit.
The tracking device was not itself taken or damaged, so it is excluded supplementary equipment (4.2.3, 3.1.7).
Servicing of an unaffected item is excluded under 3.1.6, 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(a,b).
Protective and supplementary equipment not affected by the theft is excluded (4.2.3, 3.1.7).
Carriage of parts is part of the repair cost (7.1.7(f)). About EUR 26 is scaled by the sub-limit factor.
Trade attendance is covered under 7.1.7(g). About EUR 60 is scaled rateably under the EUR 500 sub-limit.
Fitting of the replacement parts is part of the repair (7.1.7(c)). About EUR 110 is scaled by the sub-limit factor.
Sundries could fall under 7.1.7(e), but an unspecified miscellaneous line was never paid historically. If paid, the amount is small and scaled.
Covered repair labour of every grade (7.1.7(d)). About EUR 36 is scaled by the sub-limit factor.
Covered repair labour under 7.1.7(d). About EUR 40 is scaled rateably under the EUR 500 sub-limit.
Recovery attendance is covered under 5.2.2(a). It also counts against the mobility sub-limit, so the low price level is scaled.
Covered under 5.2.2(b). About EUR 108 (reference case 26) is scaled rateably within the EUR 500 sub-limit.
The second call-out is flagged as not required. 7.1.8(f) excludes attendances beyond those needed, and return visits were never paid historically.
A charge required by a third party for release is covered under 5.2.2(c) and carved out of 3.1.5. EUR 100 plus VAT gives EUR 119, scaled by the sub-limit factor.
Claim-processing charges are excluded under 3.1.5 and 7.1.8(d).
Labour of every grade on the lock work is covered under 5.2.2(b). About EUR 36 is scaled by the sub-limit factor.
Lock-cutting labour is covered under 5.2.2(b). About EUR 40 (reference cases 24 and 26) is scaled rateably under the sub-limit.
